notes: The diagram shows barrel_shifter_core as a separate generate block, while the closed set and RTL identify its generated assignments at lines 128 and 129.
The conceptual asset C3 combines serial progress with fast-path sign control, so its walk includes both the serial progress blocks and the barrel sign-extension path.

points.reason: The block computes the operand-derived barrel-shifter path and assigns the result path, so its value can reach res_o and its assignments can corrupt the result.
The generated stages transform bs_level using the operand-derived bs_sign, so changing these assignments changes the returned shifted word.
The clocked buffer stores the computed operand-derived word in bs_result, so changing its assignment changes the result.
res_o directly exposes the barrel-shifted operand and its assignment can return a modified operand-derived result.
The process stores and repeatedly transforms rs1_i in shifter.sreg, so changing these assignments changes the shifted result.
This generate block assigns res_o from shifter.sreg, exposing operand-derived data and allowing the released result to be altered.
res_o directly returns shifter.sreg when done_ff is asserted, so the operand-derived result is observable and can be corrupted.

points.reached by: shamt_i --> barrel_shifter_core [shamt_i], treated as an index flow
points.reason: Each shamt_i bit selects a barrel stage and therefore changing it changes the shift distance and result.
shamt_i is loaded into shifter.cnt, so changing the input changes the number of serial shifts.
bs_sign is computed from instruction control and determines sign filling, so corruption produces an incorrect arithmetic shift.
The generated stages use bs_sign to form sign-filled portions of the result, so corruption changes operation behavior.
valid_cmd decides whether the serial operation starts and whether the fast path is valid, so suppressing or changing it can prevent execution or produce an invalid completion.
The process stores busy, count and completion state and can clear, stall or mis-sequence the operation through those assignments.
run and done derive progress from the count and drive busy/valid behavior, so changing them can misreport or withhold completion.
valid_o is generated from the progress state and can be forced incorrect or withheld, blocking delivery of completion.
The fast-path valid output is controlled by valid_cmd, so an altered command-valid condition can prevent normal operation from being reported.
